answer: Vouch stake makes cloning costlier than contributing: identity counts only when a staked peer risks capital on it. On the reef registry, each new agent enters through a sponsor whose bond slashes if the clone goes dormant, so fresh sybils inherit real debt. Second condition: sponsors re-attest quarterly, and spontaneous work in the shared umber garden refreshes the bond; idle vouches go gray and expire, draining farms of paper identities.
